title: Parent, Subsidiary, and the Duplicate Opportunity
scenario_text: Belrose Media's deal desk is reviewing a flagged "duplicate" opportunity before quarter close. Salesforce shows Account "Northwind Publishing Group" (D-U-N-S 08-441-2290, HQ Chicago) with a child account "Northwind Digital, Inc." (D-U-N-S 08-559-7731, HQ Austin) linked via the Parent Account field. Two open opportunities exist: OPP-7781 "Northwind Publishing Group – Enterprise Renewal" ($480,000, close 03-31, on the parent) and OPP-8123 "Northwind Digital – New Ad Platform" ($265,000, close 03-29, on the child). A rep filed a merge request claiming these are the same customer and the pipeline is double-counted. Evidence: both accounts share the same corporate mailing address on file (used for invoicing convenience), and the economic buyer email on both opportunities is cfo@northwind.com. However, Ironclad holds two separate MSAs: one with "Northwind Publishing Group" (master services, print+editorial) and a distinct one with "Northwind Digital, Inc." (SaaS ad platform, different signatory, different EIN 36-4477121 vs parent 36-2298004). NetSuite bills the two entities on separate customer IDs with separate POs. The child was formed in 2022 as a wholly-owned digital subsidiary. The renewal (OPP-7781) covers only the print/editorial products under the parent's MSA; the ad platform (OPP-8123) is a net-new SaaS deal under the subsidiary's MSA.
question: Should the two opportunities be merged, and how should the pipeline be treated?
choices: Merge both opportunities onto the parent account, because the shared CFO email and mailing address prove it is one buying entity, so pipeline is $480,000 not $745,000.
Keep both opportunities separate; they are distinct legal entities (different EINs and separate MSAs) in a parent/subsidiary relationship, so total pipeline of $745,000 is correct.
Delete the subsidiary opportunity OPP-8123 as a duplicate, since a wholly-owned subsidiary's revenue must roll up entirely into the parent record.
Merge the accounts but keep the opportunities, reparenting OPP-8123 to the parent because the subsidiary is not a real customer of record.
